subject: Follow-up: Node churn impact on reserved capacity — customer escalation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Service impact to your reserved pool — immediate summary & mitigation

Samir,

I wanted to reach you first with a concise summary of what happened and what we did in the immediate window. Thank you for the quick flag this morning — I know this impacted EdgeCommerce traffic during your morning peak.

What happened (high level):
- Between 06:20–06:55 PDT we observed a cluster-level node churn event in the us-west reserved pool that triggered an autoscaler feedback loop.
- The combination of ephemeral GPU node reboots and the allocator retry logic caused request queuing and elevated latency (p90 increased from ~120ms to ~2.2s) and a spike in 5xx responses for a subset of routed traffic (~15% of requests to your reserved pool).

Immediate actions we took:
- Manually paused autoscaler resizing at 06:32 and forced a rebalance across healthy nodes.
- Deployed a hotfix to reduce aggressive re-add attempts that were thrashing the allocator at 06:40.
- Added temporary warm capacity (burst buffer) to your pool at 06:45 to clear queues and restore steady throughput.

Impact window: 06:18–06:52 PDT. We consider the pool stable as of 06:55 PDT and continued to monitor.

Attachments included with this mail: incident_timeline.csv and initial_evidence_snaps.txt (short traces + driver logs).

Next steps we propose:
1) Joint RCA call (30–45m) this week to walk through timeline and customer-visible effects.
2) Formal postmortem with root cause, remediation steps, and proposed compensation.
3) Temporary autoscaler tuning for your tenant (we can target fewer aggressive re-adds and higher headroom during your peak window).

I’ll loop in Neha and Ben for technical follow-up; Camila is copied for commercial considerations. If you have immediate questions or need raw logs for your team, say the word and we’ll prioritize.

—
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: EdgeCommerce Ops <ops@edgecommerce.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: root cause, remediation, and compensation

Samir — thanks again for the patience while we completed our initial internal triage. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the actions we will take with you.

Executive summary:
- Root cause (short): a transient GPU driver rebind sequence on a subset of recently provisioned nodes caused those nodes to report degraded health. The autoscaler’s aggressive re-add logic interpreted the transient flaps as capacity loss and attempted rapid replacement. Those re-adds interacted poorly with the allocator retry path, creating temporary request queuing and elevated 5xx rates for routed traffic. In short: driver flaps -> autoscaler thrash -> allocator queueing.

What we observed (evidence):
- Driver rebind events spiked at 06:19:41–06:22:07 PDT on 7 nodes in us-west reserved cluster (attached raw traces in logs_evidence.tar.gz).
- Autoscaler triggered 4 sequential re-add attempts between 06:24–06:30 (see incident_timeline.csv).
- Queuing and elevated latency were aligned to those re-add attempts; p95 latency peaked ~2.9s for affected requests.

Remediation (short & tactical):
1) Immediate (completed): paused autoscaler aggressive path and added warm buffer capacity to clear request backlog (06:32–06:45).
2) Near-term (deployed): patched allocator backoff logic to avoid hard thrash when multiple re-add events occur within a 90s window — rollout completed to us-west at 13:10 PDT on Oct 17.
3) Medium-term (scheduled): adjust autoscaler heuristics to prefer stabilization delay for nodes with recent driver binds; add a pre-check that small transient driver rebinds do not immediately surface as capacity loss. Canary scheduled for Oct 20.

Customer-specific mitigations we propose for EdgeCommerce:
- Immediate: one-week service credit to offset the revenue impact during the outage window. Draft credit_offer.pdf attached.
- Technical: enable a dedicated autoscaler profile for your tenant that includes +10% headroom during your morning peak and a reduced re-add aggressiveness; we will test in canary then roll to your reserved pool.
- Joint RCA call: propose Tue Oct 21, 10:00–10:45 PDT. We’ll walk timeline, evidence, and planned fixes.

Attachments: postmortem_summary.pdf, logs_evidence.tar.gz, credit_offer.pdf (draft)

Ask: Please confirm if the compensation and the proposed call time work for your team. Also let us know if you want the raw node traces and request-level ids for specific failed transactions.

Again, I’m really sorry this hit you during peak; our ops and infra teams have prioritized the stabilization work and we will share the full formal RCA after the canary completes.

Best,
